statement: crates/enforcer-memory/src/code_graph.rs, src/analysis/query.rs, src/parsers/mod.rs, and the src/languages/*.rs extractors were under heavy concurrent edit from another lane (landing a SymbolKind rich-vocabulary extension: Method/Class/Struct/Interface/Enum/TypeAlias/Module/Lambda/Variable/Constant on top of the original Function/Type/Test) while x06-a1 was implementing complexity metrics in parallel. Non-exhaustive-match compile breaks appeared and self-resolved/were fixed transiently multiple times during the session as that lane's commits landed incrementally.
why: So a future reader of this stream understands why the diff touches code_graph.rs/query.rs beyond the claimed complexity.rs/unit_complexity.rs files, and why some intermediate compile states during this session were broken through no fault of x06-a1's own changes.
howToApply: When claiming a narrow lane inside a crate with other concurrently-active lanes touching shared files (code_graph.rs, query.rs, parsers/mod.rs), poll/rebuild before editing shared structs, prefer additive field/match-arm extensions, and message primary with observed churn rather than silently reverting or fighting the other lane's edits.

statement: X06 core parity complexity metrics landed as: crates/enforcer-memory/src/complexity.rs (new, language-neutral NodeKindTable-driven AST walk for Tier A metrics: complexity/cognitive/loop_count/loop_depth/param_count/max_access_depth/linear_scan_in_loop/alloc_in_loop/self_recursive/recursion_in_loop/unguarded_recursion, plus Tier B propagate_transitive_loop_depth as a memoized, cycle-safe, depth-capped DFS over a CallGraphNode slice), additive metrics/transitive_metrics fields on SymbolNode (code_graph.rs), a CodeGraph::propagate_complexity post-index pass wired into index_repository_at_mode, and 13 new resolve_property arms in analysis/query.rs (plus an OrderKey fix so ORDER BY sorts numeric properties numerically, not lexicographically -- a pre-existing bug the mission's exact `ORDER BY f.transitive_loop_depth DESC` example would have silently mis-sorted).
why: Ground truth for the property names/semantics came from docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/refs/x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md §4.5 and the C baseline source (codebase-memory-mcp/src/pipeline/pass_parallel.c::build_def_props for Tier A, pass_complexity.c::cbm_pipeline_pass_complexity for Tier B's tld_dfs memoized-DFS-with-cycle-breaking algorithm) -- read directly rather than guessed.
howToApply: A future wave-B language adds one NodeKindTable::for_x() constructor plus one ComplexityLanguage variant + match arm in code_graph.rs::complexity_language -- no changes to complexity.rs's walk logic itself.

statement: CallEdge (code_graph.rs) is file-scoped (from_file_id + callee text), not symbol-scoped -- no language extractor currently tracks which function a call expression sits inside, only which file. CodeGraph::propagate_complexity works around this by treating every callable symbol in a file as a potential caller of every same-named callable symbol anywhere in the graph reachable via that file's call edges -- an over-approximation, not a precise call graph.
why: transitive_loop_depth is explicitly documented (both in the C baseline and this crate's complexity.rs doc comment) as an upper-bound heuristic / bottleneck candidate signal, not a proof, so over-approximating callers is the correct failure direction for now; but a future lane wanting a precise interprocedural call graph (for CALLS edge accuracy generally, not just this metric) needs to add a from_symbol_id field to CallEdge and thread the enclosing-function context through every language extractor's call-expression walk.
howToApply: Before trusting transitive_loop_depth for anything beyond 'where should I look first', check whether the caller's file also defines an unrelated same-named function -- that is the known false-positive shape.
